content.key_idea: EXIST layers three cooperative modules across a Kubernetes cluster/node/OS/hardware stack: cluster-level coverage optimization, node-level control-operation elimination, and hardware-level buffer allocation, jointly minimizing tracing overhead.

summary: EXIST is a low-overhead intra-service tracing system for datacenter applications built on hardware tracing capabilities. This figure gives EXIST's overall design overview across a Kubernetes deployment: at the cluster level, the Kubernetes Master runs the Coverage Optimizer (Sec 3.4), whose Spatial Sampler and Temporal Decider pick tracing coverage and periods from anomaly signals and user config, then push software knowledge and tracing configuration down to each node. At the node level, the Kubernetes Worker layers traced Services, a Tracing Controller (Sec 3.2, with Kernel Hooker and Tracing Facility) that minimizes costly control operations, an Efficient Tracing Abstraction over the OS, and hardware Tracer Cores with a Memory Allocator (Sec 3.3, Coreset Sampler plus Buffer Manager) that manages per-core trace buffers, producing structured trace output back to the user. Solid lines denote control paths and dotted lines denote data paths.
